Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: 55 houses destroyed and many others damaged
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The Bahamas section: 'Collectively between North Point, James Cistern, and Gregory Town on Eleuthera, the storm destroyed 55 houses and damaged many others.'
The Bahamas section: 'Despite Category 4 winds on Spanish Wells, only five houses were destroyed, although most of the remaining dwellings lost their roofs.'
The Bahamas section: 'On Grand Bahama, where a 9-to-12‐foot‐high storm surge was reported, half of the houses were destroyed, as were 13 boats and two planes, and most docks were wrecked.'
Florida header: 'Across southeastern Florida, the hurricane damaged 6,465 houses and destroyed another 383, causing over $3 million in damage.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Garages and isolated structures partly or totally destroyed, along with a lumber warehouse; some homes lost roofing shingles and suffered water damage
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: South Florida header: 'At West Palm Beach, the majority of the damage was confined to vegetation. Some garages and isolated structures, mostly lightweight, were partly or totally destroyed, along with a lumber warehouse. Some homes that lost roofing shingles had water damage to their interiors as well.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Extensive breakage of windows and loss of tile and shingle roofing
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: South Florida header: 'Nearby Lake Worth sustained extensive breakage of windows, including plate glass, and loss of tile and shingle roofing, but preparations reduced losses to just several thousand dollars.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Damage details – homes leveled; approximately 75% of roofs damaged; third floor of a building (bowling alley/Stuart News) destroyed; Walter Kitching store collapsed; old laundromat leveled; private airport destroyed; water tower downed; apartments and large hotels damaged; county jail lost all walls
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Treasure Coast header: 'At Stuart, winds removed or badly damaged three‐quarters of the roofs in town. The storm destroyed the third floor of the building that housed a bowling alley and the Stuart News, a local newspaper. In Stuart, the storm left 400 to 500 people homeless. A major landmark, the multi‐story Walter Kitching store, collapsed during the storm. An old laundromat was likewise leveled, a private airport destroyed, and a water tower downed. Apartments and large hotels also incurred significant damage. The county jail lost all its walls.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Old Olympia Inn leveled; gas station leveled; second floor of pharmaceutical building destroyed; roof of an ice plant torn off; bridge partly wrecked; nearby home leveled
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Treasure Coast header: 'Just to the south, at Olympia, an abandoned settlement also known as Olympia Beach, strong winds leveled the old Olympia Inn, a gas station, and the second floor of a pharmaceutical building. Winds also tore the roof off an ice plant. A bridge leading to the barrier island from Olympia was partly wrecked; the bridge tender survived by gripping the railing during the storm. Winds leveled his nearby home.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Many homes left uninhabitable and a 10‐car garage flattened
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Treasure Coast header: 'At Hobe Sound, which experienced the storm's eye for five minutes, the hurricane inflicted severe damage and was considered by lifelong residents the worst storm in 50 years. The storm left many homes in Hobe Sound uninhabitable, forcing crews to tear them down. A 10‐car garage at the Island Inn was flattened.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Store severely damaged; riverfront two‐story home leveled; well‐constructed home sustained only superficial damage; most small houses lost roofs or shifted; Niagara Fruit Company outbuildings lost and main house severely damaged
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Treasure Coast header: 'At Palm City the storm badly damaged structures and crops. A store sustained damage to such a degree that it was unusable, and a riverfront two‐story home was leveled; on the latter's grounds all palm trees were downed. A well‐constructed home, one of the sturdiest in Palm City, incurred only superficial damage, however. Most small houses in the area lost their roofs or were shifted on their foundations. The Niagara Fruit Company lost all its outbuildings and sustained severe damage to its main house.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Most large properties rendered uninhabitable; a number of smaller homes destroyed; citrus trees prostrated; several properties submerged from river overflow
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Treasure Coast header: 'At Tropical Farms most large properties were rendered uninhabitable, while a number of smaller homes were destroyed. Citrus trees, mainly grapefruit and orange, were prostrated, and the St. Lucie River overflowed its banks, submersing several properties.'

Treasure Coast header: 'At Sewall's Point mansions were mostly negligibly damaged, except for losses of ornamental vegetation. 40‐foot‐tall queen palms were felled, along with many tall coconut palms; several of the latter species were also left standing at an incline. Dozens of Australian pines were leveled as well.'

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: Outbuildings such as sheds, garages, and shacks wrecked; larger structures suffered little damage
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Treasure Coast header: 'Inland, at Indiantown, the storm wrecked outbuildings such as sheds, garages, and shacks, but otherwise did little damage to larger structures.'
Elsewhere header: 'High rainfall caused flooding across Florida, notably near Tampa where waters reached 9 ft deep. Over 50 homes were flooded, forcing about 150 people to evacuate.'
